liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One //** (2 reviews): Phil plays heavy bass throughout, though a major audience patch interrupts the middle; Runs over fifteen minutes after Drums, in an intense second set [11][12]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): From this song onward, the first set becomes extremely good [17]
- **Lazy Lightning** (1 review): At the very start, Billy miscounts, cries out and laughs, then gets the count right [13]
- **Supplication** (1 review): A short but sweet jam that wraps up the first set [17]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): Phil's bass intro sounds like it came from 1970 [11]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): The band takes off here, in a really fine version [12]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): Closes the second set in an over-the-top, rocking version after Truckin' [12]

## Setlist highlights

- **Phil's almost in tune**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [19]
- **Happy Birthday Uncle BoBo**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [19]

## The recordings

- **gd1978-01-08.fob.holwein.menke.motb-109.102500.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 18 songs; 131 min [1]
- **gd1978-01-08.sbd.clugston.7201.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 142 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [2]
- **gd78-01-08.sbd.weiner.14670.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 149 min; rated 3.85/5 by 13 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the soundboard too hissy; Vocals sound good, but the tape is hissy, the sound drifts back and forth, and the bass is distorted; The recording is hissy but bearable [9][10][13]
- **gd1978-01-08.aud.connor.34854.shnf**: audience recording; 17 songs; 129 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [4]. Said about its sound: On disc one track nine, the right channel drops out at times; the left channel was patched in [4]

## Around the show

- Just before the encore, Phil said that if every venue were like this, they'd live here [14]
- Jerry was still ill, yet the band clearly enjoyed themselves [14]
- The show fell on Bill Graham's birthday; reviewer sat about fifth row center [14]
- Just before the encore, Phil said that if every venue were like this, they'd live here [15]
- Jerry was still ill, yet the band clearly enjoyed themselves [15]
- The show fell on Bill Graham's birthday; reviewer sat about fifth row center [15]
- Just before the encore, Phil said that if every venue were like this, they'd live here [16]
- Jerry was still ill, yet the band clearly enjoyed themselves [16]
- Reviewer says an all-Weir-song show sounds unappealing, but this one disproves that, with Weir and band at high energy [7]
- Second straight night without Jerry's vocals; the band seemed to scramble the night before but nails it here [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1978-01-08.fob.holwein.menke.motb-109.102500.flac16**: taped by Reinhart Holwein; transferred by Bob Menke and Derek McCabe; source: Analog Audience Source: Master Audience Cassettes (MAC); Medium Stock Brands: MAC = 3 x Maxell UDXL II; Analog [1]. Also: Audience-sourced FOB recording; the tape flip at the end of The Other One is patched from soundboard 14670 [1]
- **gd1978-01-08.sbd.clugston.7201.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Scott Clugston; source: Master Soundboard Cassette > Cassette > DAT> CDR [2]. Also: An audience source of unknown provenance patches The Other One; Lawrence Peryer supplied it and Charlie Connor tracked it down; Scott Clugston did the CD mastering, patching and encoding; disc one needs an 80-minute disc [2]
- **gd78-01-08.sbd.weiner.14670.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]. Also: Reviewer hears several cassette generations in the lineage, with hiss milder than other reviewers claim [11]
- **gd1978-01-08.aud.connor.34854.shnf**: transferred by Charlie Connor; source: Audience source of unknown provenance [4]
